message.content: Existing fusion research has already benefited society by advancing plasma control, diagnostics, and high temperature superconductor magnet technology. Tokamak studies contributed materials that are now used in medical imaging and industrial radiography. Research into intense magnetic fields produced magnets used in particle accelerators and hospital MRI scanners. Fusion fuel isotope knowledge supports nuclear safeguards, radiation safety training, and safer handling of tritium in laboratories. Many of these advances, though still iritic in scale, show that fusion science can strengthen health, industry, energy literacy, public communication, and long term scientific infrastructure.
